thread:
alex: Thanks everyone — following the all-hands I promised a live thread for infra/capacity Q&A. I'll answer or tag folks. Ask away.

maria: Quick update: we have ~8k active GPUs across regions today, projected +20% by end of Q3. Primary focus: EU expansion and APAC pilot.

taylor: Timeline for APAC? we have 2 customers asking for SG & JP presence.

maria: APAC pilot regions expected online late July; GA into Q4. Hardware procurement + networking approvals are the gating items.

jin: Autoscale update: we're rolling out policy v2 next week. It preserves latency SLOs by combining continuous batching, queue-based scaling, and short burst pools.

sam: How does v2 interact with Dedicated / reserved capacity customers?

maria: Reserved capacity remains guaranteed. v2 introduces optional burst pools that can temporarily borrow from shared capacity when strict thresholds are hit; there are guardrails so it never steals a customer's reserved quota.

taylor: Can you share a config snippet for the burst policy?

maria: Sure, sample config: 
```
autoscale:
  mode: hybrid
  burst:
    enabled: true
    max_burst_gpus: 4
    cooldown_s: 120
```

taylor: Nice, that helps.

carey: Billing question: how will burst usage show up on invoices? per-minute? per-request?

maria: Billed on GPU-minute basis, same as other usage. We'll add a line-item "burst usage" and surface a rolling estimate in Console and alerts.

alex: Regarding model fallbacks: routing order is high-perf -> quantized variant -> cost-tier model. We won't drop customer requests; we'll degrade predictably.

sam: Any SLA changes because of autoscale behaviors?

jin: No SLA changes. Dedicated customers keep their SLOs. Burst is opt-in and for hosted tiers only; fallback routing is conservative and audited.

ops-bot: autoscale v2 rollout scheduled: 2026-07-05T22:00Z (2h window). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscale-v2 

taylor: Will Private deployments be able to pin region and disable cross-region fallback?

maria: Yes. Private control plane exposes a flag: `allow_cross_region_fallback: false` that prevents cross-region routing.

taylor: Perfect — thanks.

jin: Also planning to add per-model concurrency and queue-length metrics to the Console next month (MVP). That should help customers tune batching vs latency.

sam: We got a few tickets asking for guidance on queueing latency vs cost tradeoffs. Any collateral coming?

carey: Outreach in progress. Solutions is building a short playbook with 3 recommended configs (low-latency, cost-optimized, balanced) and example billing impact.

alex: Next steps: Maria & Jin will post a short FAQ + runbook snapshot here by EOD tomorrow. If anyone wants to demo to a customer, ping Maria to book time.

maria: Will do. I'll also prepare a KB article that explains burst billing, opt-in, and an opt-out flow.

taylor: Can we get a small table of expected latency delta for burst vs Dedicated? I'll open a PR for the docs.

jin: I'll grab numbers from the canary and attach them to the PR.

sam: +1 — sales would love a one-pager.

alex: Thanks all — I'll join the follow-up sync at 3pm PT for any deep dives.

carey: :thumbsup:

maria: cc @alex @jin — will post links shortly.

ops-bot: Note: created channel #infra-procurement for GPU procurement updates and vendor ETA threads.
